title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Handyman
audience: Handyman operators who complete several small fixed tasks in one visit for landlords, property managers and households, including sole traders.
learningOutcomes: Write a visit offer that names the tasks, the time frame, the exclusions and the return-visit term
Show what certainty and protection the price includes, and what it does not
Price the offer from value and cost, then compare it with published vendor ranges

instruction.heading: Sell a visit with a result, not an hourly rate
instruction.body: A handyman's customer often has a list: a sticking door, two shelves, a gate latch. An offer of 'handyman at a set hourly rate' leaves the customer unable to predict the bill. An offer such as 'we complete up to six listed tasks in one visit, finish by a stated time, photograph each finished item, and return within 14 days at no charge for any listed item not finished' gives the customer a result and a limit. The 14 days is an example. Set your own period and check that you can keep it.

instruction.heading: Use three levels that each add something visible
instruction.body: A good, better and best structure suits a handyman when each level adds something the customer can see: a small visit for up to three listed tasks, a larger visit for up to six, and a half-day block. A Queensland vendor listing gives half-day handyman jobs at $250 to $500 and full days at $500 to $960 (The Quote Yard, QLD, published 10 May 2026). That is a vendor estimate, not regulator data. Set your prices from your own cost first and use the vendor range only as a check. A non-trade pricing experiment (INSEAD, October 2025) found that many buyers chose the middle option. Treat that as a hypothesis to test in your own quotes.

instruction.heading: Put scope, exclusions and one total in writing
instruction.body: List each task, the materials you supply, the materials the customer buys, and what is excluded, such as electrical circuit work, plumbing, structural repairs and any rot found behind a fixing. A written quote binds once it is accepted, so the exclusions protect the price. Show one total and say whether GST is included. Once registered for GST, the ATO says the selling price should include GST, and the registration threshold is $75,000 of GST turnover. In Western Australia, extra work needs the customer's permission first, and a tradesperson cannot do extra work and then ask for payment later.

instruction.heading: Offer guarantees you can afford
instruction.body: Consumer guarantees apply to services and cannot be removed by contract. A service must be done with due care and skill, and a business should get a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault. A stated fix-first policy for listed tasks is therefore a useful promise. A 'no refunds' line does not override those rights. Keep any extra guarantee to what you control, such as a return visit, and do not promise a result you cannot measure.

instruction.heading: Price from value, then check cost
instruction.body: A higher price is easier to justify when the customer gets one visit that clears the list, a finish time, a photo record and a return visit. Price from that outcome, then check the figure against your cost per productive hour and the travel and set-up time in the visit. Business.gov.au guidance says a quote should recover every cost and add a margin, so the premium only counts once the cost is covered.

procedure: Write the outcome of the visit in one sentence a customer would repeat.
List the tasks the visit covers, the maximum number, and the finish time you can keep.
Write the exclusions and the materials the customer must buy or provide.
Add one certainty element, such as a photo of each finished item, and set the return-visit period.
Set the package price from your cost, then check it against the vendor range for the same tasks and state GST status.
Confirm the offer in writing and record the answer, and check the offer again after the first ten visits.

workedExamples.situation: A property manager sends a handyman a list of four items for one rental: a sticking bathroom door, two bedroom shelves, a loose gate latch and a loose towel rail. The scenario is illustrative.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which package should the handyman offer, what should it exclude, and what price basis should it show?
workedExamples.reasoning: The four items fit within a visit of up to six listed tasks, so the middle package suits the job. The gate latch is offered as a task only if the gate post is sound; a damaged post is excluded and quoted separately. Vendor estimates for the same tasks are a door adjustment at $100 to $200, basic shelving at $100 to $250, and a simple gate repair at $120 to $300 (The Quote Yard, QLD, published 10 May 2026). These are vendor estimates and are not used as the price. The handyman sets the total from his own cost and margin, shows one total with GST status, and writes the 14-day return-visit term into the offer. The price is not stated in this lesson because it depends on the owner's own figures.

equipmentAndPpe: Offer template with tasks, exclusions, time frame and return-visit term
Photo checklist for each finished item
Quote sheet showing GST status and a validity date
PPE as set by the site's own rules and {{business:safety.required_ppe}}

commonErrors.error: Quoting an hourly rate for a list of small tasks
commonErrors.prevention: Quote one visit package with the listed tasks, the finish time and the exclusions.

commonErrors.error: Promising a result or a repair you cannot afford
commonErrors.prevention: Limit the guarantee to a return visit for listed items and a fix-first window you have set.

commonErrors.error: Leaving out GST status, travel or the materials the customer buys
commonErrors.prevention: Show one all-in total, state whether GST is included, and list travel and materials in the offer.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. The ACCC says misleading statements about prices are prohibited. Check its current wording before publishing package prices. This lesson does not grant any licence, registration or authority.

Licence thresholds are set by each state, and they are not the same. In Queensland, building work above $3,300 including materials, labour and GST needs a licence (QBCC). In NSW, minor maintenance above $5,000 in labour and materials including GST needs a licence. Check your state before you offer a package that could cross the line.

Victoria: a written major domestic building contract is needed for work over $10,000 (Consumer Victoria). The home-warranty insurance threshold is unresolved. One Consumer Victoria page gives $16,000, and another gives $20,000 from 1 July 2026. Check which figure applies before you quote Victorian work.

Electrical and plumbing work requires licensed tradespeople. Vendor sources disagree about which handyman tasks fall under that rule, so refer any wiring, gas or drainage task out and say so in the offer.

qualityStandard: Every package lists its tasks, time frame, exclusions and return-visit term.
Every quote shows one total with GST status and a validity date.
Every extra task is priced and approved in writing before it is done.
documentationEvidence: Written package offer with tasks, exclusions and time frame
summary: Sell a visit with a result, a finish time and a return-visit term, not an hour.
Show one total, the exclusions and the GST status.
Price from value, then check the price against your cost.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of a handyman's offer does the customer buy?
options: Your hourly rate on its own
The outcome, with a time frame and certainty
How many years you have been in business

knowledgeChecks.question: What should the guarantee in a visit package be?
options: Something you can deliver and afford
Impossible to claim on in any case
Available only to friends of the business

knowledgeChecks.question: A customer asks for an extra task while you are on site. What must happen first?
options: Do the task and invoice it later
Get the customer's permission and price the extra work in writing first
Add it to the next visit without telling the customer
Ask a neighbour whether the customer can afford it
